name: p5.brush
role: Natural-media brushes, wash fills, hatching and flow-field strokes for p5.js sketches
summary: p5.brush 3.x adds pencils, charcoal, markers, watercolour-style fills, hatch patterns and vector fields that bend strokes to a p5 WEBGL canvas (a standalone build needs no p5). In VCR a scene clears and redraws from scratch at each seek with its seeds reset, so the hand-drawn look captures deterministically with alpha.
use_when: Hand-drawn illustration, hatching or print look for generative stills and motion in a browser scene
Over rough-js when fills, hatching or flow-field strokes are needed; over p5-js alone, which has no brush or fill model
A p5-js scene that should look like pencil, charcoal or watercolour
avoid_when: Plotter or pen-path output: vsketch or vpype
Many frames at speed: brush fills ran at roughly 5 frames per second here
Plain procedural shapes with no media look: p5-js
notes: 2026-11-27: the lead said 3.0.0; npm latest is 3.3.0 (published 2026-11-26), and that is the version the fixture ran.

assessment.rationale: MIT; npm 3.3.0 published 2026-11-26, repository active; peer p5 ^2.2 (standalone build needs none). Fills the hand-drawn media gap that rough-js (no fills or flow fields) and p5-js (no brush model) leave. The p5 build needs a WEBGL canvas and seeds must be reset each frame, both of which the fixture handled.

evidence.result: 90 alpha frames at 1280x720, 90 unique frame hashes, shuffled order matches sequential; frames 0, 30, 60 alpha min 0 max 1; frames inspected (wash disc with hatching, moving flow lines).
evidence.scope: p5.brush 3.3.0 on p5 2.3.4 WEBGL in Chromium via @vcr/capture, macOS arm64: hatch, wash fill, flowLine, marker rect at one seed; not the standalone build, buffers or hardware GPU.
